analysis: Documentation-only batch: changelog.d/feature-waitlists.md (new, head 1-7) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head 182, 191, 1360-1385, 1635-1727). Both describe a new `darkbloom waitlist` command and a client-side waitlist gate before new `sandbox setup` and new `darkbloom cluster` pairing. The documented behavior: GET/POST /v1/waitlists[/{feature}] carrying the login token as a Bearer credential (A-008); https-only or loopback http; no redirects; 10 s timeout; 64 KiB cap; POST body {}, so no Mac data is sent; terminal control/bidi characters in coordinator text are replaced. A 404 fails open (setup continues). Existing pairings and add-ons are never asked, and `cluster local` is ungated. This gate is a CLI-side UX/policy check that runs on an adversarial provider Mac (ADV-001, TB-003), so a local operator can trivially bypass it. Actual feature authorization must therefore be coordinator/platform-enforced; the docs do not claim otherwise. It does not weaken TB-013/T-061, since installer download controls are unchanged and only renumbered as step 3. It does not touch TB-014/T-062 either. Swift sources are not in this batch: Waitlist/WaitlistCommand.swift, FeatureWaitlist.swift, FeatureWaitlistView.swift, FeatureWaitlistGate.swift, SandboxSetupCommand.swift (SandboxSetupFlow.requireApproval) and ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift (requireNewPairApproval). Integration must verify those sources: token sent only to the configured https/loopback coordinator with redirects disabled (token leak risk to A-008); the response size/timeout limits; terminal sanitization of coordinator strings; and that the 404 fail-open and unreadable-pairing bypass match the docs. The threat model may need a note that waitlist approval is not a security boundary on the provider side. No regression is identified from the documentation alone.
